title: Why We Chose VLESS-Reality Over WireGuard, OpenVPN and Shadowsocks
metaTitle: Why Doppler Uses VLESS-Reality Instead of WireGuard or OpenVPN
metaDescription: How we chose a protocol for networks that block VPNs: fixed fingerprints, active probing and block lists, why WireGuard, OpenVPN, Shadowsocks and Trojan fell short, and the trade-offs we accepted.
excerpt: Three questions decided it: does the protocol have a fixed fingerprint, what do probes see, and is there anything to block by name? Here is how each option answered, and what we gave up.

faq.question: Why doesn't Doppler use WireGuard?
faq.answer: WireGuard's fixed-size handshake is easy for filters to recognise, and carriers in Russia have been reported cutting it. Doppler is built for networks like that, so we use VLESS-Reality, which looks like ordinary TLS to a real website.

faq.question: Is VLESS-Reality slower than WireGuard?
faq.answer: On a clean connection the difference is small. On lossy networks WireGuard's UDP transport can be faster. VLESS-Reality's advantage is that it keeps working where WireGuard is blocked.

faq.question: Can VLESS-Reality be blocked?
faq.answer: Yes, it is not a guarantee. Research has shown TLS-inside-TLS can be fingerprinted and some Russian ISPs were reported cutting Reality connections in November 2025. We adjust server settings as filtering changes.

faq.question: Which platforms does Doppler support?
faq.answer: Doppler has apps for iOS, Android, macOS and Windows.
